messages:
anya: Quick question for the group — should we aim for a single uniform routing policy surface for all tenants, or allow per-tenant localized policy overlays? Trying to weigh operability vs flexibility.

matt: I'm leaning uniform-first. Easier to reason about, test, and explain to customers. But worried about edge cases for enterprise tenants who need custom fallbacks.

sylvia: Agreed on uniform-first, but we need a clear escape hatch. Maybe a two-layer model: core policy + tenant overlay that can only set a small whitelist of overrides.

kevin: If we do overlays we need to define what can be overridden. Overrides cause combinatorial explosion in verification. Any override that affects scoring functions (cost/latency) will break assumptions in autoscaler.

anya: Good point. Autoscaler assumes monotonic cost metrics. If tenant overrides custom penalty curves we could get weird admission behavior.

matt: Ops cost also matters — extra config surface means more bug reports. How about this proposal sketch: 

```
# policy v2 sketch
core_policy:
  - prefer: low_latency
  - fallbacks: [regional, lower-tier]
overlay_allowed_fields: [region_preference, max_cost_multiplier]
overlay_blocked_fields: [penalty_curve, admission_filters]
```

This keeps core decisions central but allows tenant hints.

kevin: I like the concrete allowed/blocked whitelist. We should also attach a runtime validation step that rejects overlays that violate invariants. infra-bot: policy-linter v0.9 will add validation hook for overlay schema.

anya: What telemetry contract do we need so we can detect when overlays cause SLA regressions? We need per-tenant p95 latency, cost-per-1k tokens, and fallback-rate.

sylvia: Also we should emit a "policy-override-applied" event with reason and diff so audits can trace a request back to an override. That helps security/compliance.

matt: Rollout plan: 1) implement core-only uniform policies, 2) add overlay scaffolding and linter, 3) dogfood overlays for internal accounts, 4) gated release to customers behind feature flag.

kevin: Can we simulate overlays in the policy-sim harness before allowing them? i.e. run tenant overlay through a synthetic traffic profile and compare metrics. If p95 increases > 5% or fallback rate > 1% fail the check.

anya: Yes — add simulation gate. Also need a canary window where overrides are limited to <1% of traffic and we monitor cost & quality.

matt: Who owns the invariants? Need a small spec: monotonicity of cost function, no admission filter changes, and region-affinity must be additive-only. That should be product + infra-led.

sylvia: UI/UX question: how do we present overlay restrictions in the console? Suggest showing allowed fields with inline examples and a preview simulation button.

kevin: Implementation notes: prefer overlays implemented as a delta YAML that merges at evaluation time. Keep merging deterministic and cheap — no full policy recompilation on every request. Cache merged policies per-tenant with TTL and invalidation on overlay update.

anya: Edgecases: what if overlay references a model variant not available in the region? policy should validate model compatibility against catalog at overlay submit time, not at eval time.

matt: Also think about rollback semantics: overlays should support "dry-run=true" and a clear revert path. We can't let customers shoot themselves in the foot.

anya: Action items:
- kevin: draft overlay schema + linter rules (due EOD Thu)
- sylvia: telemetry event spec + dashboard mock (due Mon)
- matt: rollout plan doc & canary thresholds (due Fri)
- anya: add simulation gate to policy-sim and define pass/fail thresholds (due next Wed)

kevin: noted. I'll start with allowed/blocked fields list and add unit tests for monotonicity checks.

sylvia: I'll wire up a lightweight dashboard mock and include example failure alerts (spike in fallback-rate).

matt: Thanks all. If no objections I'll start a short RFC PR with the two-layer proposal and sample overlays. :thumbsup:

anya: No objections from me. One more thing — let's define a small set of "blessed overrides" for enterprise customers (region pinning, short-term burst allowance) and keep everything else blocked.

kevin: +1. Keeping the set small will make verification manageable.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: rfc-overlay-schema -> policy-sim -> telemetry-dashboard -> dogfood flag.

matt: Great. We'll sync after RFC PR.
